title: Paloma and the Summit
premise: Kestrel Whitlock, who learned to read riverbeds instead of their estranged archaeologist mother's letters, is hired as a digger on a salvage expedition upriver — only to discover the missing team they've been sent to find includes their mother. Racing a rival salvage fleet to a sunken temple wreck, Kestrel must choose between the treasure that could buy their freedom and the crew of misfits who have quietly become family. When the fleet's captain reveals he intends to strip the site and silence witnesses, Kestrel leads a desperate six-tide gambit to raise the temple's keystone and flood the salvage channel behind them. In the end, Kestrel loses the treasure but gains a name of their own — signed, for the first time, at the bottom of the expedition report.
about_author: Ulyana Halloran is a former river guide who spent a decade running cargo through remote tributaries before turning her hand to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who measure life in miles, drawing on her love of waterways, wrecks, and found families.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Working a dredging contract in a muddy port town, Kestrel takes a job escorting an upriver expedition after its radio goes silent — telling themselves it's just pay, not that the missing team list bears their mother's name. The emotional beat: guarded competence masking seven years of unspoken grief.

chapters.title: The Silent Reach
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The expedition boat pushes into fog-choked narrows where the radio crackles with half-words; they find the mother's camp abandoned mid-meal, instruments still recording. Kestrel realizes someone left in a hurry — or was taken. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into reluctant hope that she's alive.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, joined by diver Marisol and engineer Bo. Decoding the mother's field notes, they learn the wreck lies beneath a tidal siphon that opens only six tides per season — and a black-hulled salvage fleet is already anchored downstream. Emotional beat: the crew coalescing around a shared, impossible deadline.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. First dive through the siphon reveals the temple wreck intact but booby-trapped by the mother's own collapse-lines — she sealed it deliberately. Marisol surfaces with a carved token bearing Kestrel's childhood nickname. Emotional beat: wonder laced with the first hint that the mother left messages meant for Kestrel alone.

chapters.title: The Black-Hulled Fleet
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Captain Vess of the salvage fleet boards under a flag of parley, offering partnership and revealing he knows Kestrel's parentage — and intends to use it. Bo refuses, but the encounter costs them their winch cable. Emotional beat: humiliation curdling into defiance as the crew sees Vess's true ambition.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Trapped by a storm in a cliff cave, Kestrel finds the mother's cache: seven years of unsent letters explaining why she left, and why she sealed the wreck — to keep a corrupt patron from weaponizing what's inside. Emotional beat: anger breaking open into understanding, identity reframed as chosen rather than inherited.

chapters.title: The Siphon Turns
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. With three tides left, the crew attempts the deep dive; Bo's patched rig fails, and Marisol is caught in the siphon's pull, saved only by Kestrel diving after her against all protocol. They recover the keystone map but lose their last air reserves. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into trust — Kestrel chooses people over self-preservation.

chapters.title: Vess's Bargain
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Vess captures the camp, offering Kestrel command of the salvage and their mother's freedom in exchange for the keystone route. Kestrel pretends to accept, feeding him a false channel while the crew rigs the siphon gates. Emotional beat: cold clarity — power offered is power corrupted, and Kestrel refuses to become Vess.

chapters.title: Raising the Keystone
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. The climax: on the final tide, the crew raises the keystone through the siphon as Vess's fleet enters the false channel; the gates open and the river swallows his ships whole. Kestrel reaches their mother in the flooded lower vault as the waters rise. Emotional beat: breathless sacrifice rewarded — reunion amid ruin.

chapters.title: A Name of Their Own
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Weeks later, the crew files the expedition report together: the wreck documented, the treasure ceded to the river authority, Vess's patrons exposed. Kestrel signs the report — Whitlock, but written in their own hand — and agrees to lead the next survey upstream. Emotional beat: quiet arrival home, in a family made rather than given.
